title: Casefile extract v2
description: One record per casefile. Replaces casefile-extract v1: no per-mail records, no titles or summaries. The record is built incrementally - mails are fetched 5 at a time in pagenum order (window 6, stride 5), each window's mail bodies and content-bearing attachments are read, and equipment[], problems[], faults[] and action_logs[] are UPDATED in place (ids from earlier windows are never dropped or renumbered) until progress.complete is true. Every value is read from the fetched pages[].link bodies and attachment bytes, never from the export's summary fields. Mail digests and attachment digests live in their own collections; this record references them by mail_id / attachment_sha only.

casefile_id.description: MongoDB _id of the casefile; the identity of the record.

vessel_name.description: Audit only, and the stopword source for subject-stem normalisation. Never an identity.

extraction_version.description: Prompt+schema version that produced this record (03 §6). Bumped whenever either changes.

progress.description: Resume cursor for the windowed build. Not a statistic: it says where the next window starts.

last_pagenum_processed.description: Highest pages[].pagenum whose mail and attachments have been folded in. -1 before the first window.

complete.description: True once every page of the casefile has been processed and consolidate has run.

problem_statement.description: ONE line, 10-15 words, the core problem of the casefile. Read from attachments (SOF, service/defect reports) where they exist. Written at consolidate, after the last window.

export_meta.description: Copied verbatim from the casefile export for audit and traceability. Never filter, group or extract on these.

equipment.description: Every piece of equipment a fault or action refers to, once each. Maker/model/serial only if a document states them, else "NA". Never inferred from vessel class or sister ships.

problems.description: Concluded causes, one row each, with their own p-ids. A fault links to at most one problem via faults[].problem_id; several faults may share one problem (one cause, symptoms on two cylinders). A problem exists only when a document CONCLUDES it; suspicions are not problems.

faults.description: The things being fixed: one row per (symptom, equipment[, problem]) triple. Every action points at exactly one fault. A casefile is not one case - KING ONE carries four. A symptom that returns after a resolved action or a stated gap is a NEW row linked by recurrence_of.

action_logs.description: One row per action occurrence, in seq order. Built window by window: a new action is appended with the mail that announced it; an outcome reported in a later window UPDATES the existing row (late binding) and never creates a new one. See docs/05.

validation_flags.description: Set by the deterministic validator (02 §2.4): dropped_object, unresolved_fault_id, quote_not_found, over_cap. Empty when clean.

shortId.description: Short in-record id: e1.. equipment, p1.. problems, f1.. faults, a1.. actions. Assigned by the extractor in order of first appearance; stable across windows, never renumbered; the loader prefixes them with casefile_id for a global key.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD as stated or clearly implied by the mail/document; null if not stated. Never estimated.

mail_ids.description: Mails (pages[].referenceId) whose body or attachments state this.

attachment_shas.description: The attachment(s) the evidence_quote was copied from, when the source is a document rather than the mail body. One quote, the documents that state it — attachments that evidence a later update live in supporting[].

evidence_quote.description: Verbatim text from the cited mail or document. The validator checks it occurs there. No quote, no assertion.

supporting.description: Evidence for later UPDATES to the row (an outcome, a maker/model, a concluded cause), one entry per update: its own mails, its own attachment, its own verbatim quote. Keeps the row's primary quote tied only to the documents that state it. Optional; validated like the primary quote.

fields.description: Which fields of the row this entry evidences (outcome, maker, problem_id, ...), or merged_from:<id> when it is the evidence of a row merged into this one.

name.description: As the documents call it, e.g. 'Starboard main engine'.

equipment_type.description: Free text type for the resolver: main_engine, auxiliary_engine, boiler, purifier, ...

position.description: stbd | port | No.2 | ... when the vessel has more than one.

details.description: Components, part numbers, running hours, software version as stated.

symptom.description: The failure mode as a short phrase (≤6 words: what is wrong, e.g. 'knocking sound', 'water leak', 'fails to start'); which unit / where goes in `position`; the full sentence as written goes in provenance.evidence_quote.

alarms.description: Machine-generated alarm texts, verbatim, if any.

position.description: Where on the equipment: 'cyl 5', 'No.5 and No.6 exhaust bellows'.

problem_id.description: Link to problems[].problem_id once a document concludes the cause. null while undetermined - expected to be common. Filled in place on the existing fault; never a new fault.

suspected_cause.description: A cause someone suspects but no document concludes ('C/E blames poor ME quality'). Never promoted to problem_id by the extractor.

recurrence_of.description: fault_id of the earlier fault this one is a RETURN of: the same symptom on the same equipment, reported again after an action on the earlier fault was stated as resolved or after a stated gap of normal operation. null for a first occurrence. Optional (additive in v2); a recurrence is its own row with its own dates, evidence and actions.

fault.description: The (symptom, equipment) pair being fixed, linked to a problem row once one is concluded. Actions point here.

fault_id.description: The fault this action was mainly taken against. One event is one row: other faults the same single event also serves are listed in also_fault_ids, not copied into rows of their own.

also_fault_ids.description: Other faults the same single event also serves (one request to the maker covering two cylinders, one service attendance quoted for three pending issues). Optional; never contains fault_id. The loader fans the action out to these faults if it needs per-fault rows.

seq.description: Order within the casefile by date_performed, else date_reported. Assigned at consolidate.

occurrence_no.description: 1 the first time this action is taken on this fault; 2 if repeated.

target.description: Sub-location the action was applied to ('cyl 5', 'No.1 crosshead bearing'). Distinguishes a retry from the fault spreading.

action.description: What was done, one line, as the mail states it.

advised_by_org.description: Organisation whose instruction the action followed, if stated.

parts.description: Part names / numbers used, as stated.

date_performed.description: When the action was carried out, if stated.

asserted_in_mail.description: The mail (or the mail carrying the document) that first announced the action.

finding.description: Diagnostic actions only: what the test showed, as stated.

outcome.description: What a mail STATES happened after the action. unknown is a value and the expected majority; a vague mail stays unknown. Corrective/preventive/administrative/commercial use resolved|partial|no_effect|made_worse|unknown; diagnostic uses conclusive|inconclusive|no_information|unknown.

verification.description: none only when value is unknown.

outcome_in_mail.description: The mail that states the outcome. Usually later than asserted_in_mail. null when unknown.

outcome_date.description: When the outcome was observed, if stated; else that mail's date; null when unknown.

evidence_quote.description: Verbatim from outcome_in_mail. Required whenever value != unknown.

statement.description: The cause as the document states it: 'idler gear free-end bearing severely worn, thrust collars broken'.

asserted_by.description: Who concluded it. A suspicion does not create a problem row.
